items: The year is now guessed together with the performers and the piece. Each guess can include a year; within 2 years counts, and a wrong year tells you whether to go earlier or later. Sooner is worth more: 2 points on the first two tries, then 1.5, then 1.
Naming the right composer no longer earns a point or saves a try once the composer hint has been shown.
Audio now stops when you switch to another tab, instead of playing on.
Dropped the piano-roll brand name from the player and the hints. The first hint now gives the composer's dates instead.

title: Cleanup
items: Performers listed under two names are merged, such as Eugenie Adam and Eugenie Adam-Benard.
Fame ratings fixed: studio orchestras no longer count as famous.
A set of pieces no longer appears beside its own numbered pieces. For example, Chopin's Op. 28 now lists Preludes Nos. 1–24, and a roll of several preludes accepts any of them.
Titles in other languages and other spellings of the same work count as one answer, such as Arabeske and Arabesque.
Composers use their usual short names, such as Beethoven rather than van Beethoven.
Popular songs, dance music and instrumental solos were removed. Lieder and other classical art songs have their own genre.

title: Opera, orchestral music and practice
items: Added about 900 opera, orchestral and art song records from the Library of Congress, alongside the piano rolls.
New Practice tab with filters for format, genre, recording years and how famous the composer and performer are.
Each puzzle plays a random part of the piece, and only misses lengthen the clip.
The piece box searches about 8,800 works as you type.
The roll display never shows notes past the part you've unlocked.

title: Launch
items: Whose Hands launched with 450 piano rolls recorded between 1905 and 1925.
